description: Early monastic site, thought to date back to the late 6th CE. The earliest stone building (thought to be a church) excavated could only be dated between the 7th - 11th CE, but disturbed earlier 6th - 7th CE deposits, which have been used to suggest an earlier, possibly 6th CE church. This would also line up well with the life of the patron, and possibly founder Saint Ernán. The island's name translates to "The isle of Marnock", itself a derivation of Mo Ernóc, a pet name of Ernán, this is seemingly corroborated by a 7th CE slate excavated from an enclosure ditch that had the name Ernán inscribed onto it. This seemingly confirms Ernán as the patron saint, if not the founder.
bibliography: Lowe, Christopher, and Daniel Atkinson. Inchmarnock: An Early Historic Island Monastery and Its Archaeological Landscape. Edinburgh: Society of Antiquaries of Scotland, 2008.

Ó Carragáin, Tomás. Making Christian Landscapes in Atlantic Europe: Conversion and Consolidation in the Early Middle Ages, 2017.
